name: Avestan
notes: Avestan, the liturgical language of the Zoroastrian Avesta (Old Avestan ~1000 BCE Gathas, Younger Avestan later composition layer), an Eastern Iranian language natively written in the Avestan script (a highly phonetic ~53-letter alphabet, right-to-left, devised in Sasanian times specifically to render the oral liturgy precisely). Per repo convention for ancient languages with a non-Latin native script (cf. akk.json, pal.json), this spec is scored in the standard Hoffmann scholarly transliteration (Hoffmann 1971, refined in Hoffmann & Forssman 2004) rather than the native script itself; `orthography_kind` is set to `transliteration` because the transliteration is a letter-by-letter scholarly re-encoding with no independent standards body, not a native orthography people read and write. CONSONANTS follow the Hoffmann letter values: stops ⟨p b t d k g⟩, palatal affricates ⟨č ǰ⟩ = /tʃ dʒ/, fricatives ⟨f β θ δ s z š ž ṣ̌ š́ x xʷ γ h⟩ (Avestan retains archaic voiced fricatives β δ γ rather than the aspirate series of Old Indo-Aryan), nasals ⟨m n ń ŋ ŋʷ⟩, trill ⟨r⟩, semivowels ⟨y v⟩ = /j w/ (with ⟨ii uu⟩ as the corresponding non-syllabic diphthong-final spellings). VOWELS: 16-quality system with a length opposition throughout (⟨a ā⟩, ⟨i ī⟩, ⟨u ū⟩, ⟨e ē⟩, ⟨o ō⟩, ⟨ə ə̄⟩), the back rounded ⟨å ā̊⟩ = /ɒ(ː)/, and nasalised ⟨ą ą̇⟩ = /ã(ː)/. Beekes (1988) analyses [ð] and [ɣ] as Old-Avestan allophones of /θ/ and /x/ (per Wikipedia 'Avestan phonology', fetched); not enumerated as separate positional rules here for lack of a clean context statement, but recorded as allophones. VALIDATION NOTE (2026-08): the full Hoffmann transliteration letter set and IPA values used in this spec (vowels a ā å ā̊ ą ə e o i u with length/nasal series; consonants p b t d k g č ǰ f β θ δ s z š ž ṣ̌ š́ x xʷ γ h y v r m n ń ŋ ŋʷ) were checked directly against Skjærvø's (2007) 'Old Iranian' chapter (Table 3.1.5 Avestan alphabet, Table 3.2.1 vowels, Table 3.2.2 consonants) — the Encyclopaedia Iranica articles by the same author blocked WebFetch with HTTP 403 both directly and via archive.org, so this chapter (identical scholarly authorship and content) was used as the actually-fetched primary source. Every grapheme in this spec's letter inventory is attested in Skjærvø's tables; no corrections to the transliteration mapping were needed.

ancestors.notes: Descent from Proto-Iranian (Eastern Iranian branch); sister of Old Persian, not descended from it.

location.notes: Approximate homeland of the Avestan liturgical tradition, eastern Iranian world (Bactria/greater Khorasan area); no fixed point since the Avesta's geography is disputed.
